ideal_weight_faq1_a: The Robinson formula (1983) is the most commonly used and generally most accurate for most people. Miller is a more modern alternative, Devine is the original formula, and Hamwi is more conservative.
ideal_weight_faq2_a: Each formula was developed based on different population studies and uses different coefficients. Differences of 5-10 kg are normal and all are valid estimates.
ideal_weight_faq3_a: Ideal weight is only a guideline. It doesn't account for muscle mass, bone structure, age, or health condition. The healthy BMI range (18.5-24.9) is often more accurate.
ideal_weight_faq4_a: Ideal weight formulas calculate a specific weight for your height. BMI is the ratio of weight to height squared and provides a range of healthy weights.

irr_faq_3_a: Net Present Value (NPV) is the difference between the present value of income and expenses. A positive NPV indicates a profitable investment.
irr_faq_4_a: The payback period is the time required for cumulative cash flows to cover the initial investment. A shorter period is better.

privacy_policy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy_policy.content:
Last updated: 2/20/2026

1. Introduction
Welcome to MathCalc Pro. We are committed to protecting your personal information and your right to privacy. This privacy policy applies to all information collected through our website.

2. Data Collection
We only collect information that you voluntarily provide to us when you contact us via email. This includes your email address and the content of your message.

3. Automatically Collected Information
When you visit, use, or navigate the site, we automatically collect certain information. This information does not reveal your specific identity (like your name or contact information) but may include device and usage information, such as your IP address, browser and device characteristics, operating system, language preferences, referring URLs, device name, country, location, and information about how and when you use our website.

4. Third-Party Services
We use Google Analytics to analyze website traffic and Google AdSense to serve advertisements. These services use cookies to collect and process data. Google's use of data is described in their privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites

5. Your Rights
Depending on your location (e.g., EEA, UK, California), you have certain rights regarding your personal data, including the right to request access, correction, or deletion of your data. You can exercise these rights by contacting us.

6. Imprint / Operator
The website is operated by an independent professional (OSVČ) based in the Czech Republic. For privacy inquiries or requests, please contact: info@mathcalc-pro.com.

roi_examples_desc: Practical examples of return on investment calculation
roi_faq_1_a: Return on Investment (ROI) is a financial metric that measures the efficiency of an investment as the ratio of profit to the invested amount.
roi_faq_2_a: A good ROI depends on the industry and risk. Generally, 7-10% annually is solid, 15%+ is excellent. Compare with alternative investments.
roi_faq_3_a: Total ROI covers the entire period, while annual ROI is annualized. Annual ROI enables comparison of investments with different durations.
roi_faq_3_q: Difference between total and annual ROI?
roi_faq_4_a: Fees, commissions, taxes, maintenance, insurance, and all other costs associated with the investment for an accurate ROI calculation.

time_examples_description: Practical uses of the time calculator
time_faq_1_a: Times are converted to seconds, added together, and the result is converted back to hours:minutes:seconds. If minutes or seconds exceed 59, they automatically carry over to the next unit.
time_faq_2_a: The calculator automatically returns the absolute value of the difference, so the result is always positive. For example, 1:00:00 - 2:00:00 = 1:00:00.
time_faq_2_q: What happens when subtracting a larger time?
time_faq_3_a: Yes, the calculator supports times up to 999 hours, which is useful for calculating project times, monthly working hours, etc.
time_faq_3_q: Can I calculate with more than 24 hours?
time_faq_4_a: Add all working segments together or subtract the start time from the end time. The calculator automatically handles carry-overs between units.

time_formula_description: Times are converted to seconds, the operation is performed, and the result is converted back to HH:MM:SS format.

tip_faq_1_a: In restaurants, 15-18% is standard. For exceptional service, 20% or more is appreciated. At bars and cafes, rounding up or 5-10% is acceptable.
tip_faq_1_q: How much tip should I give?
tip_faq_2_a: If service was genuinely poor, you can tip less (5%) or nothing, but it's considerate to explain your decision.
tip_faq_3_a: Divide the total amount (bill + tip) by the number of people. The calculator automatically shows the amount per person including their share of the tip.
tip_faq_3_q: How do I split the bill among multiple people?
tip_faq_4_a: Tip is typically calculated on the total bill amount including taxes. This is the total amount you pay for food and beverages.

unit_converter_description: Convert between different units of length, weight, volume, and temperature
unit_converter_example_3_desc: A cook needs to convert 250 g to ounces for an American recipe.
unit_converter_example_4_desc: Converting 2 liters of milk to US cups for baking.
unit_converter_example_5_desc: A physics student needs to convert room temperature of 22 °C to Kelvin.
unit_converter_faq_1_a: Each unit has a conversion factor to a base unit. Conversion is done by converting to the base unit and then to the target unit.
unit_converter_faq_2_a: Temperature requires special formulas (not just multiplication) because scales have different zero points and different intervals.
unit_converter_faq_3_a: We support length (mm, cm, m, km, in, ft, yd, mi), weight (mg, g, kg, t, oz, lb), volume (ml, l, m³ and imperial), and temperature (°C, °F, K).
unit_converter_faq_4_a: To convert °C to °F, use the formula: °F = °C x 9/5 + 32. For example, 20 °C = 20 x 1.8 + 32 = 68 °F. To convert back: °C = (°F - 32) x 5/9.
unit_converter_faq_4_q: How do I convert Celsius to Fahrenheit?
unit_converter_faq_5_a: The metric system (SI) uses meters, kilograms, and liters, and is based on powers of 10. The imperial system uses feet, pounds, and gallons, and is common in the US and UK. Most of the world uses the metric system.
unit_converter_faq_5_q: What is the difference between metric and imperial units?
unit_converter_faq_6_a: One US gallon equals approximately 3.785 liters. A British (imperial) gallon is larger at approximately 4.546 liters. Our converter uses the US gallon, which is more common in international contexts.
unit_converter_faq_6_q: How many liters are in a gallon?
unit_converter_faq_7_a: The results are mathematically precise based on defined conversion factors. For length, weight, and volume, exact multiplication factors are used. For temperature, precise formulas are applied for converting between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin scales.
unit_converter_faq_7_q: How accurate are the conversion results?
unit_converter_formula_temp_desc: Temperature conversions require special formulas because temperature scales have different zero points. For length, weight, and volume, simple multiplication by conversion factors is used.
unit_converter_seo_description: Free unit converter. Convert between length, weight, volume, and temperature units. Fast and accurate conversions.

x_percent_of_y_description: Calculate what percentage one value represents of another. Perfect for calculating discounts, test scores, and percentage ratios.

x_percent_of_y_faq_1_answer: Divide value X by value Y and multiply by 100. Formula: (X ÷ Y) × 100 = result in percentage.
x_percent_of_y_faq_1_question: How do I calculate what percentage X is of Y?
x_percent_of_y_faq_2_answer: This calculation is commonly used for calculating discounts, test scores, ratios, percentage representation, and other practical situations.
x_percent_of_y_faq_3_answer: The result will be greater than 100%. This means that value X is greater than value Y. For example, 150 is 150% of 100.
x_percent_of_y_faq_3_question: What if X is greater than Y?
x_percent_of_y_faq_4_answer: No, value Y cannot be zero because it would result in division by zero, which is mathematically undefined.
x_percent_of_y_formula_description: The percentage is calculated as the ratio of value X to value Y multiplied by one hundred.
x_percent_of_y_interpretation_equal: Value X is equal to value Y.
x_percent_of_y_interpretation_less: Value X represents a smaller part of value Y.
x_percent_of_y_interpretation_more: Value X is greater than value Y.

y_x_hundred_faq1_a: The formula is: (Y ÷ X) × 100. If you know the part (Y) and its percentage share (X), you can calculate the total value (100%).
y_x_hundred_faq1_q: How does the Y is X% - what is 100% calculation work?
y_x_hundred_faq2_a: For example, when calculating the original price before a discount, the total budget from a partial amount, or the total count from a percentage sample.
y_x_hundred_faq2_q: When should I use this type of calculation?
y_x_hundred_faq3_a: Yes, after obtaining the total value (100%), you can verify that the given part (Y) actually corresponds to the given percentage share (X%).

- Advertising Cookies: We use third-party vendors, including Google, which use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to our website or other websites.
